_comment: The trajectory calculation as pinned (docs/CONTEXT.md §Calculation spec, BOOTSTRAP.md §6,
issue #73). The suite reads this file and keeps no copy of the numbers.
`parameters`: the fixture-wide defaults. `warm_up_days` pins State to afloat while
days_elapsed < warm_up_days. `drifting_below` and `taking_on_water_below` are dimensionless
multipliers of the Baseline Daily Budget (B): State compares Trajectory Variance (V) against
threshold x B directly, with no division, so a non-terminating B never enters the comparison
as a rounded number. Any `figures` row may override any of the three via its own
`warm_up_days` / `drifting_below` / `taking_on_water_below` fields.
`figures` rows: symbols follow CONTEXT.md's table (P=daily_pool, D=period_days,
e=days_elapsed, S_settled=settled_spend, S_today=today_spend, S_future=future_spend). Every
money figure is a 4dp string. `forward_daily_rate` is null exactly when r = D - e = 1 (the
last day of the Period), per CONTEXT's 'undefined on the last day' rule. Every allowance
figure (baseline_daily_budget, todays_allowance, forward_daily_rate) is floored toward -inf at
4dp (R1); left_to_spend_today is floored A minus the exact S_today, never independently
rounded. trajectory_variance and buffer_days go on the wire half-up (half away from zero) at
4dp (R2), computed from exact values, never from another figure's rounded output.
`target_line` rows: the mid-period Budget change from CONTEXT §Mid-period Budget changes.
`effective_day` is 1-indexed (`j`); T(j-1) is the cumulative target through day j-1 under the
old baseline. `expected.targets` lists the cumulative target at specific days, half-up at 4dp;
`expected.baseline_after` is the new baseline (B_new), floored at 4dp, and may be zero or
negative when the clamp engages (P_new <= T(j-1)) - the target line itself stays flat at
T(j-1) for the rest of the Period in that case, never dipping below it.
Every expected value here was computed independently in exact rational arithmetic (Python's
fractions.Fraction) and cross-checked against Python's decimal module with ROUND_FLOOR /
ROUND_HALF_UP, not derived from the backend's implementation.
Rows added with issue #155 PR 2 (the calculation, a formula change): the existing rows above are
unchanged and still hold, since a Period whose Daily Pool never changed has T(e) = B x e.
A `figures` row may carry `base_daily_pool` and `changes` (a list of {effective_day, daily_pool}):
the Daily Pool the Period began with and each later change. `daily_pool` is then the pool in force
Today (day e+1), which is what the dashboard passes as P; the test checks the two agree. The target
line is built from the list, and Trajectory Variance is V = T(e) - S_settled; Buffer Days and the
State thresholds are read against B_now, the slope in force Today; fixed-mode A = B_now. Every
segment's slope is max(slope, 0), the first included, so a pool at or below zero is a flat target
at zero and a later raise starts from the flat value. A change effective on day 1 replaces the base,
two changes on one day are one (the later wins) and a change to the pool already in force merges away.
P' = P - max(S_future, 0): a refund dated in the future never raises the Available Pool.
`fully_committed: true` in `expected` means the baseline in force is zero: there is then no State,
no baseline_daily_budget, no trajectory_variance and no buffer_days (the keys are absent), while
available_pool, todays_allowance (fixed mode: 0), left_to_spend_today and forward_daily_rate are
still answered. That is the target line's situation and says nothing about money: a row whose
todays_allowance is zero or negative with a healthy baseline is an Available Pool used up, and its
State is computed as usual.
`target_line_changes` rows: the list shape. `inputs` are the Period's `period_days`, its
`base_daily_pool` and `changes`; `expected.points` lists, at chosen days, the cumulative `target`
(half-up at 4dp) and the `baseline` in force that day (floored at 4dp, clamped at zero).
The `target_line` rows keep their single-change shape; a test runs them through the list as well.
The new rows were computed independently in exact rational arithmetic (Python's fractions.Fraction,
a separate implementation of the line, the clamp and the State), and V = r x (A_adaptive - B_now)
was asserted for every row with no future-dated spend, every change in force and an unclamped last
segment.
